descriptors.R: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1953
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1933 to 1953 and has held a majority in Congress since the 1954 elections

compile_desc.R: the party of the administration in office since 1953
compile_desc.D: the party that held the presidency from 1933 to 1953 and has held a majority in Congress since the 1954 elections

others_line: Other choices on some ballots, including unpledged elector slates in parts of the South and National States' Rights and Socialist Labor nominees (answer "other").
never_name: Nixon, Kennedy, Johnson, Lodge, Eisenhower, Byrd, Thurmond, Goldwater, Faubus or Truman

slice_sources.men: 1960 census (April) carried to November 1960 along the 1950→1960 trend; men 21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky, 19+ in Alaska, 20+ in Hawaii) outside the eleven Southern states, in the 50 states (first election with Alaska and Hawaii; no presidential vote in DC); calibrated to certified 1960 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1960 census (April) carried to November 1960 along the 1950→1960 trend; women 21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky, 19+ in Alaska, 20+ in Hawaii) outside the eleven Southern states, in the 50 states (first election with Alaska and Hawaii; no presidential vote in DC); calibrated to certified 1960 returns.
slice_sources.south-white: 1960 census (April) carried to November 1960 along the 1950→1960 trend; white adults (21+ (18+ in Georgia and Kentucky, 19+ in Alaska, 20+ in Hawaii)) in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults), where poll taxes still applied in Alabama, Arkansas, Mississippi, Texas and Virginia; calibrated to certified 1960 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1960 census (April) carried to November 1960 along the 1950→1960 trend; Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; registration held to under a third of Black adults by literacy tests, poll taxes, registrar discretion and intimidation. The shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1960 census (April) carried to November 1960 along the 1950→1960 trend; foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized citizens (aliens could not vote in any state).

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
